2. Short facts leading to this Rule are that the petitioner claimed to be the sole owner of the premises No. 52/1 Patla Khan Lane, Dacca and that he has been in possession of the premises in part performance of an agreement for sale entered into between him and the original owner in 1951. By notice dated 1-4-73 the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South) Dacca (respondent No. 2) asked the petitioner to surrender possession of the said premises to one Kamaluddin Ahmed (respondent No. 3) and the petitioner on enquiry came to learn that the order had been passed on the application filed by respondent No. 3 for restoration of possession of the said house on the allegation that he had abandoned the said those on 27-3-71 and the petitioner taking advantage of the situation had taken forcible possession of the same. On the said complaint a Miscellaneous Case being No. 16 of 1972 was started which was finally disposed of by the Officer-in-charge of the abandoned property by his order dated 22-4-72 on the finding that the premises in question was not an abandoned property. Thereafter, the petitioner was surprised to receive another notice dated 3-4-73 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South) Dacca (respondent No. 2) asking him to surrender possession of the said house to respondent No. 3 under President's Order No. 13 of 1972. The petitioner thereafter made enquiries and came to learn that the respondent No. 3 had filed a petition on 15-2-72 before the Sub-Divisional Officer, Dacca which was sent to the Chairman, Farashgonj Arbitration Court by respondent No. 2 for disposal and an ex-parte order was passed by the said Arbitration Court 6-8-72. Without the knowledge of the petitioner. On the basis of the said ex parte order passed by the Arbitration Court, the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South) Dacca by his order dated 21-10-72 directed issuance of the surrender notice. The petitioner's further allegation was that he never received any notice from Farashgonj Arbitration Court and the same was fraudulently suppressed by respondent No. 3 and the Sub-Divisional Officer also passed an ex-parte order without any notice to him. Thereafter on 28-4-73 the petitioner filed an application before the respondent No. 2 praying for setting aside the aforesaid order dated 21-10-72 but the said application was summarily rejected. Thereafter, the petitioner preferred an appeal and the Special Tribunal by its judgment and order dated 28-2-74 dismissed the appeal. Against the said order of dismissal the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule calling upon the respondents to show cause why the order passed by the Special Tribunal, Dacca in Tribunal Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5 of 1973 should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 (3) "On receipt of an application under clause (1), the Arbitration Court shall at first ascertain from both the parties whether they  agree to Arbitration and thereafter A shall, after such local enquiry as it may think fit and after examining the evidence oral and documentary that may be given by both the parties, find out whether the applicant is an evacuee, whether the property was in actual possession of the applicant on the specified date, and whether the property is in unauthorised occupation of the person named in the application. (4) Where the parties have agreed to Arbitration, the Arbitration Court shall, no the basis of its findings under clause (3) pass an order either allowing the prayer of the applicant or reject it ; and this order shall be final and binding on both the parties. (5) Where the parties have not agreed to Arbitration, the Arbitration Court shall send its findings under clause (3), along with the record of the case, to the Thana Magistrate, having jurisdiction for such order as he may deem fit. 

 7. From a perusal of the above provisions of law it is abundantly clear that the Arbitration Court was empowered to take evidence both oral and documentary and give their findings on the basis of the said evidence. It was therefore incumbent upon the Arbitration Court to record at least the gist of the evidence and considers the said evidence while arriving at their finding. But, from the records we do not find any recording of the evidence. Even the names of the persons who deposed on behalf of respondent No. 3 before the Arbitration Court have not been noted. The Court acting under a statute must discharge its duties in accordance with law and not in an arbitrary manner. Then again under clause (6) of Article 7 of Order as quoted above, it was the duty of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate to consider the findings of the Arbitration Court and the evidence on record and after such further enquiry as he may consider necessary or after hearing both the parties, pass an order in writing either allowing the prayer of the applicant or rejecting it. The order dated dated 21-10-72 shows that the mandatory provisions of law under clause (6) of the Article 7 have not been complied with. It was the duty of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate under the law to afford the parties an opportunity of hearing before him and then pass the final order either allowing or rejecting the grayer. In the instant case, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate did not even serve any notice on the parties, far less allow them a hearing, and passed the order as if he was passing an executive order. It was, therefore, no order in the eye of law. The learned Sub-Divisional Magistrate by his order dated 21-10-72 directed issuance of the surrender notice which, in our opinion, was a consequential order to be passed after the final order as required under clause (6) was passed. The impugned order cannot by any stretch of imagination be construed as a final order required to be passed under clause (6) of Article 7 of President's Order No. 13 of 1972. In the absence of the final order under clause (6) of Article 7, we find that the order directing surrender of the properties cannot be sustained in law. 

 11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The order of the learned Sub-Divisional Magistrate dated 21-10-72 as communicated in Memo No. 2690(2) dated 3-4-73 (Annexure 'B') and affirmed by the judgment and order dated 28-3-74 passed by the Special Tribunal in Tribunal Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5 of 1973 is hereby declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and of no legal effect. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we make no order as to costs.
